Examination shows mild abdominal distension and stool in the rectal vault. He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily, zolpidem 10 mg at bedtime, and aspirin 81 mg daily. After amlodipine titration and addition of lisinopril, her blood pressure is 118/68 seated and 114/66 standing. She feels well and reports more energy. Which interpretation of the SPRINT evidence supports continuing her tolerated regimen with monitoring?

While evaluating the new pain and delirium, the team considers acetaminophen as one component of treatment for her osteoarthritis pain. Which approach follows Hazzard’s discussion of this drug?

Which change directly removes an NSAID exposure while retaining a non-NSAID analgesic strategy?

Which description of medial branch blocks agrees with Hazzard?

He takes levodopa/carbidopa, rasagiline, amantadine, and quetiapine 50 mg at bedtime for hallucinations. Examination shows masked facies, resting tremor, and saliva pooling. A modified barium swallow shows delayed pharyngeal transit with residue; creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. Which statement explains why increasing dopaminergic medication need not improve his swallowing?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with mild parkinsonism and type 2 diabetes has six months of worsening short-stepped gait and difficulty initiating movement, without tremor. MRI shows enlarged ventricles and periventricular white-matter changes. Carbidopa-levodopa provides little benefit. CSF opening pressure is 180 mm H2O. In Hazzard’s differential of parkinsonism, which diagnosis is specifically associated with the enlarged-ventricle finding?

Practice · An 86-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced Parkinson disease is hospitalized with aspiration pneumonia. She is bedbound, needs a pureed diet, and has lost 15 lb over three months. She takes carbidopa–levodopa, quetiapine 25 mg at bedtime for hallucinations, and mirtazapine 15 mg for depression; creatinine clearance is 32 mL/min. After stabilization, her daughter asks about tube feeding. The patient and family choose comfort-focused care, and the attending physician and hospice medical director certify a terminal prognosis of less than six months if the illness follows its expected course. Which service model fits these established goals and eligibility?

Practice · A 91-year-old man with advanced Parkinson disease, dysphagia requiring a pureed diet, and recurrent aspiration pneumonia has severe constipation. He takes carbidopa/levodopa, pramipexole, and lansoprazole. He spends an hour straining on the toilet. Examination shows normal anal tone but impaired coordination of pelvic floor relaxation. Lactulose, suppositories, and enemas have not helped. His creatinine clearance is 35 mL/min. Which intervention directly targets the pelvic floor coordination problem?

Practice · An 83-year-old woman with Parkinson disease, depression and overactive bladder develops confusion and visual hallucinations. She takes carbidopa–levodopa, pramipexole, nortriptyline and solifenacin. Which medication pair contributes the greatest anticholinergic burden?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with Parkinson disease becomes confused during admission for pneumonia. He takes carbidopa–levodopa, rasagiline and pramipexole. Compared with levodopa, which complication occurs more often with dopamine agonists in older patients?

Practice · A 75-year-old man hospitalized with pneumonia has Parkinson disease, benign prostatic hyperplasia, and insomnia. He takes carbidopa-levodopa, tamsulosin, and zolpidem. He develops acute confusion and visual hallucinations, with a positive CAM screen despite stable vital signs and no fever. Which recommendation about zolpidem agrees with the 2023 Beers Criteria?

Practice · An 85-year-old man with mild Parkinson disease and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22) develops visual hallucinations and paranoid delusions. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg twice daily and pramipexole 0.5 mg three times daily. Vital signs and head CT are normal. Which medication-review conclusion follows Hazzard's comparison of dopamine agonists with levodopa?

Practice · An 82-year-old man with Parkinson disease (Hoehn-Yahr stage 3) is hospitalized after a backward fall with head injury; CT shows no acute finding. On day two his MoCA is 22/30, compared with 25/30 three months earlier. He is more confused in the evening and sees children in the room. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily and pramipexole 1 mg three times daily. Alongside evaluation for acute causes, which medication-review approach addresses a recognized contributor to hallucinations?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman develops a poorly controlled right arm over one year. She drops objects, and the arm sometimes grasps her clothes involuntarily. She has difficulty planning meals and operating the microwave. Examination shows asymmetric right-arm rigidity and dystonia, cortical sensory loss, and ideomotor apraxia. MRI shows asymmetric left frontoparietal atrophy. Six months of carbidopa-levodopa has not helped. Which clinical syndrome best describes this combination?

Practice · An 89-year-old man with advanced Parkinson disease develops rigidity and fever after running out of carbidopa-levodopa and stopping it abruptly. Which medication change is the recognized trigger of a neuroleptic malignant-like syndrome described by Hazzard?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease, hypertension and osteoarthritis is assessed after a fall in assisted living. He takes carbidopa/levodopa, amlodipine and as-needed acetaminophen. Examination shows masked facies and cogwheel rigidity, with a marked fall in blood pressure and dizziness on standing. Which approach fits the described treatment principles for orthostatic hypotension?

Practice · A 79-year-old man with longstanding Parkinson disease develops cognitive decline and visual hallucinations while taking carbidopa-levodopa, ropinirole, and amantadine. During medication review, which description of amantadine is supported by Hazzard?

Practice · An 85-year-old man with Parkinson disease and recurrent falls freezes when walking through doorways. He takes carbidopa-levodopa and quetiapine for hallucinations. Examination shows a shuffling gait, reduced arm swing, and difficulty with tandem walking. Which advice about physical therapy and cueing follows Hazzard?

Practice · A 79-year-old nursing-home resident with advanced Parkinson disease and recurrent UTIs has worsening constipation despite lactulose 30 mL daily. She has had no bowel movement for five days and reports abdominal pain. Examination shows abdominal distension and a large, firm rectal fecal impaction. She takes carbidopa/levodopa, oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily, and prophylactic trimethoprim; creatinine clearance is 35 mL/min. Before inserting rectal enemas or suppositories, what does Hazzard recommend for the firm impaction?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with advanced Parkinson disease, orthostatic hypotension, and recurrent falls is admitted after syncope. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/250 mg four times daily, midodrine 10 mg three times daily, fludrocortisone 0.1 mg daily, and tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily for BPH. Blood pressure falls from 130/80 to 88/54 on standing. His Clinical Frailty Scale score is 8/9. His daughter asks about prognosis and says he wished to avoid being kept alive by machines. Which approach to tamsulosin follows Hazzard's management of orthostatic hypotension?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease, BPH, and insomnia reports dizziness on standing and three falls in the past month. He takes carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily, terazosin 5 mg at bedtime, zolpidem 10 mg nightly, and recently added oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily. Blood pressure falls from 145/85 supine to 118/70 standing with dizziness. Which pair combines a nonselective peripheral alpha-1 blocker with a strongly anticholinergic drug in Beers 2023?

Practice · An 82-year-old man with major depression, Parkinson disease, and mild cognitive impairment has not responded to several antidepressant trials. After gradual titration over several weeks, pramipexole reaches 0.5 mg three times daily in addition to mirtazapine 30 mg nightly; he also takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg and entacapone 200 mg three times daily. Two days later, his wife reports new online gambling and inappropriate sexual comments. Which recognized dopamine-agonist adverse effect best matches these behaviors?

Practice · An 86-year-old man with Parkinson disease, BPH and recurrent falls takes carbidopa–levodopa, tamsulosin, oxybutynin and mirtazapine. He has dry mouth, severe constipation, hesitancy and a postvoid residual of 250 mL. Which medication change best addresses this combination?

Practice · An 85-year-old man is in a nursing facility for rehabilitation after a hip fracture. He has Parkinson disease and benign prostatic hyperplasia and takes carbidopa/levodopa, tamsulosin, oxycodone 5 mg every 6 hours as needed, and ferrous sulfate. He has had no bowel movement for 7 days despite daily lactulose. Abdominal radiography shows a moderate colonic stool burden, and creatinine clearance is 38 mL/min. Which option is supported for ongoing laxative treatment?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease, depression, and chronic pain from spinal stenosis attends a medication review. His wife reports increasing daytime sedation and two near-falls. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily, sertraline 100 mg daily, gabapentin 300 mg three times daily, tramadol 50 mg four times daily, and docusate 100 mg twice daily. He also takes oral diphenhydramine 50 mg nightly for sleep. Which characteristic of diphenhydramine explains the Beers recommendation to avoid this use?

Practice · An 85-year-old man is found on the kitchen floor after preparing breakfast, with no memory of the collapse. He has Parkinson disease, BPH, hypertension, and chronic back pain. He takes carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 mg four times daily, tamsulosin 0.8 mg nightly, lisinopril 20 mg daily, and tramadol 50 mg as needed. Examination shows resting tremor and bradykinesia. Which pairing correctly describes two recognized contributors to orthostatic hypotension present in this history?

Practice · An 86-year-old woman with advanced Parkinson disease, depression, and recurrent urinary tract infections attends follow-up. She lives in assisted living, uses a wheelchair, and has mild dysphagia. Her daughter reports worsening tremor and two falls this month. Medicines are carbidopa-levodopa 25/250 mg four times daily, pramipexole 1 mg three times daily, sertraline 100 mg daily, and nitrofurantoin 100 mg daily for prophylaxis. Her creatinine clearance is 28 mL/min. Which statement about nitrofurantoin follows Beers 2023?

Practice · An 80-year-old man with Parkinson disease is found confused and nearly unresponsive. Temperature is 32.5 degrees C, blood pressure 90/55, and heart rate 48. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg four times daily, pramipexole 1 mg three times daily, benztropine 1 mg twice daily, and chlorpromazine 50 mg at bedtime for chronic hiccups. Recent TSH is 4.2 and creatinine 1.8; ECG shows J waves. Rewarming has begun. Which explanation warrants a medication review while rewarming continues?

Practice · A 79-year-old man with Parkinson disease and REM sleep behavior disorder is hospitalized after his wife calls emergency services. He struck her during sleep, causing a black eye. He is distressed, has no waking history of violence, and wants to remain at home; his wife requests nursing-home placement for safety. He takes carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily and ropinirole 2 mg at bedtime. Which statement about the source’s approach to this sleep disorder is correct?

Practice · An 83-year-old man with Parkinson disease has repeated falls when turning and freezes at doorways despite carbidopa/levodopa and rasagiline. Examination shows masked facies, cogwheel rigidity and multiple small steps when turning. Which rehabilitation approach is supported for freezing of gait?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Parkinson disease and knee osteoarthritis has recurrent falls and dizziness on standing, including two falls while reaching for his walker. He takes carbidopa–levodopa 25/100 mg three times daily, pramipexole 1 mg three times daily, and celecoxib 200 mg daily. Blood pressure falls from 138/82 supine to 106/68 standing with dizziness. There is a moderate knee effusion. Which consideration supports reviewing the pramipexole dose as part of management?

Practice · גבר בן 86 עם דמנציה מעורבת (MMSE 15), CHF (EF 35%), ו-CKD שלב 3b מאושפז עם CHF לא מאוזנת. הוא מבולבל לגבי מיקום ותאריך אך מזהה בני משפחה. לבתו יש ייפוי כוח מתמשך והיא מציינת שהוא היה רוצה 'הכל'. הוא נוטל furosemide 40mg BID, carvedilol 12.5mg BID, lisinopril 5mg, ו-memantine 10mg BID. לאחר דיורזה, מצבו יציב. טיפול פליאטיבי ממליץ על הוספיס. מה הצעד הבא המתאים ביותר?

Practice · A 75-year-old woman with diabetes, heart failure (ejection fraction 40%), and chronic insomnia still has a sleep latency of 90 minutes despite CBT-I and appropriate sleep hygiene. She takes metformin 500 mg twice daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 20 mg daily. Creatinine is 1.3 mg/dL and eGFR 44 mL/min. Which listed drug is described by Hazzard as a selective melatonin-receptor agonist that reduces sleep latency?

Practice · A 92-year-old woman with COPD requiring home oxygen, heart failure (ejection fraction 35%), and chronic pain from spinal stenosis takes sustained-release morphine 15 mg twice daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 5 mg daily. She reports straining for 30 minutes and passing small, hard stools every 3–4 days. She has fallen twice in the past month while straining on the toilet. A suppository is being considered for rectal outlet delay. Which initial choice and timing follow Hazzard?

Practice · A 78-year-old man with frailty (Clinical Frailty Scale 6), heart failure (ejection fraction 35%), and stage 4 chronic kidney disease (eGFR 22) attends follow-up. His wife reports that he falls asleep during meals and forgets medications. He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, carvedilol 25 mg twice daily, and furosemide 40 mg daily. HbA1c is 7.2%, potassium 4.8, and creatinine 2.8. Which change addresses the metformin contraindication stated in Hazzard?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with HFrEF (EF 28%), moderate Alzheimer dementia, and creatinine clearance of 32 mL/min has improved after intravenous furosemide for fluid overload. Her regular medications are lisinopril 10 mg daily, carvedilol 3.125 mg twice daily, and furosemide 40 mg daily. Blood pressure is 102/58 mm Hg. Her family asks about sacubitril/valsartan. The team is assessing tolerability and whether to switch. If an ACE-inhibitor-to-ARNI switch is selected, which initiation plan follows Hazzard?

Practice · An 82-year-old woman with heart failure (EF 35%), permanent atrial fibrillation, and type 2 diabetes is admitted with volume overload. She functions independently, but her daughter reports recent difficulty managing medications. Her medications are carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 5 mg daily, furosemide 80 mg twice daily, spironolactone 25 mg daily, renal-adjusted apixaban, and metformin already withheld during acute illness. Potassium is 5.8, creatinine 1.9 (baseline 1.3), and BNP 1850. ECG shows atrial fibrillation at 78 beats/min with QRS 118 ms. Which approach to spironolactone follows Hazzard's safety guidance?

Practice · An 80-year-old woman with severe knee osteoarthritis has recurrent pain rated 7/10 that limits shopping. A course of three hyaluronic acid injections six months ago initially helped. She has heart failure with an ejection fraction of 35% and stage 3b CKD, and takes furosemide, lisinopril, and carvedilol. Examination shows an effusion and crepitus. She is reluctant to undergo the knee replacement recommended by her surgeon. Which intra-articular option has the strongest guideline support for short-term relief of her knee pain?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman is being assessed for home palliative care after three admissions in four months for heart-failure exacerbations. She has ischemic cardiomyopathy (EF 25%), stage 4 CKD (eGFR 24 mL/min/1.73 m²), and mild cognitive impairment. She takes furosemide 80 mg twice daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 5 mg daily, and spironolactone 12.5 mg daily. She lives with her daughter, who works full time. The patient says she wants “no more hospitals,” but her daughter insists on calling emergency services whenever she becomes breathless. What should be done next to address their differing care expectations?

Practice · A 73-year-old woman hospitalized with a heart failure exacerbation receives intravenous furosemide 40 mg twice daily. She has had no bowel movement since admission four days ago. Her home polyethylene glycol 17 g daily was omitted. She also takes lisinopril, carvedilol, and spironolactone and eats regular meals. Potassium is 3.8, magnesium 1.9, and creatinine 1.2. Which description correctly explains the action of polyethylene glycol if it is restarted?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with severe osteoarthritis and stage 3a CKD (eGFR 52; Cockcroft–Gault creatinine clearance 38) has inadequate relief from acetaminophen 1 g three times daily. She has hypertension and heart failure with an ejection fraction of 45%, and takes lisinopril, carvedilol, and furosemide. If an opioid trial is warranted after other treatments have been reviewed, which agent does Hazzard place before other opioids?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with diabetes, heart failure (ejection fraction 40%), and mild dementia attends a geriatric clinic. His wife reports two falls in the past month, missed medication despite pill organizers, and inability to manage household finances. She works full time and feels overwhelmed. He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. HbA1c is 9.1%, creatinine 1.6, and eGFR 42. Which model explicitly uses protocols addressing medication management, falls, dementia, and caregiver burden?

Practice · An 86-year-old man with moderate dementia, heart failure (EF 40%), and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 24; Cockcroft-Gault CrCl 22 mL/min) physically resists care and has thrown a cup at another resident. He takes donepezil 10 mg, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, and furosemide 20 mg daily. After assessing contributors and trying nonpharmacologic measures, dangerous aggression persists. If the risk-benefit assessment favors risperidone, which prescribing approach matches Hazzard?

Practice · A 77-year-old man hospitalized for a heart-failure exacerbation becomes confused at night, fails to recognize his wife and tries to leave, although he was alert and oriented that morning. His regular drugs are lisinopril, carvedilol and spironolactone; zolpidem was added three weeks ago. Assessment shows acute onset, inattention and disorganized thinking with normal alertness. Which approach addresses a potentially modifiable contributor?

Practice · An 83-year-old man with stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22), heart failure, and mild dementia is hospitalized with volume overload. During intravenous furosemide treatment he develops urinary leakage because he waits too long to reach the toilet. His oral regimen includes furosemide 40 mg twice daily, increased from once daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 5 mg daily. Postvoid residual is 30 mL and urinalysis is normal. Which description matches scheduled toileting?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (EF 35%), mild cognitive impairment, and knee osteoarthritis is hospitalized with decompensated heart failure. She lives alone and is independent in four of six activities of daily living. Her discharge medications include furosemide 40 mg twice daily, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, lisinopril 5 mg daily, and naproxen 500 mg twice daily for knee pain. Creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL and eGFR is 28 mL/min/1.73 m². If an oral analgesic is still needed after non-drug measures, which initial change best fits the approach on Hazzard p312?

Practice · An 82-year-old man with coronary disease, previous bypass surgery, diabetes, and chronic kidney disease is euvolemic after treatment of decompensated heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. He takes carvedilol, lisinopril, and furosemide. Spironolactone is being considered. Which statement follows Hazzard's description of this treatment?

Practice · An 86-year-old man with heart failure and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 22) presents after falling while gardening. He reports several days of dizziness and weakness. Medications are furosemide 80 mg twice daily, spironolactone 25 mg daily, carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 5 mg daily. Potassium is 5.8 mEq/L, creatinine 3.2 mg/dL (baseline 2.8), and BUN 78. Blood pressure is 102/58 mm Hg and pulse 52. Which change addresses the mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist contraindication described in Hazzard?

Practice · An 80-year-old woman in assisted living has moderate macular degeneration with visual acuity 20/200 and heart failure with ejection fraction 35%. She has stopped attending bingo, misses meals, and stays in bed. She takes furosemide 40 mg twice daily, carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, and lisinopril 20 mg daily. Potassium is 3.2 and creatinine 1.4, compared with a baseline of 1.0. Alongside assessment of these medical findings, which environmental plan follows Hazzard's low-vision recommendations?

Practice · An 81-year-old woman with stage 4 CKD, heart failure, and mixed urinary incontinence takes furosemide, carvedilol, and lisinopril. Since starting darifenacin she has had little improvement in urgency and troublesome constipation requiring daily laxatives. Her daughter asks about increasing darifenacin. Which medication-review principle should guide the discussion?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with heart failure (ejection fraction 35%), stage 3a chronic kidney disease (eGFR 45), and chronic insomnia is seen after a fall at home. He has taken zolpidem 10 mg nightly for a year, prescribed by his previous physician. He also takes furosemide, lisinopril, carvedilol, and aspirin. His wife reports morning confusion and two falls in the past month while getting up to use the toilet. Blood pressure is 140/80 supine and 110/65 standing. After medication review, a supervised zolpidem discontinuation plan is made. Which treatment should form the basis of ongoing insomnia care according to Hazzard?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with moderate vascular dementia, heart failure (ejection fraction 35%), and stage 3 CKD has slept more, eaten less, and stopped watching television over two weeks. He takes carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, and citalopram 20 mg daily, started three weeks ago. He has flat affect and psychomotor slowing; sodium is 128, potassium 3.8, and creatinine 1.6. Which approach addresses a recognized medication-related contributor before attributing the change to chronic disease?

Practice · An 85-year-old man with mild dementia (MMSE 22), hypertension, and stage 3a chronic kidney disease (eGFR 45) has developed increasing difficulty managing finances, finding his way to familiar places, and taking medications over three weeks. His wife died six months ago. His daughter asks about supported accommodation, but he wants to remain at home. Examination and routine laboratory results are normal. Alongside evaluation of this recent change, which approach directly assesses whether his home setting can meet his current needs?

Practice · An 81-year-old woman with moderate Alzheimer dementia is admitted from assisted living for pneumonia. On day three, she becomes disoriented and tries to leave. She previously managed basic ADLs independently but now needs dressing assistance. She takes donepezil 10 mg, sertraline 50 mg, and IV ceftriaxone. Vital signs are stable; WBC is 14,000, creatinine 0.9, and electrolytes normal. While assessing acute precipitants, which initial symptom-management approach fits Hazzard?
Practice · A man with Alzheimer disease reports poor sleep after starting donepezil. Which accompanying finding would support another recognized adverse effect of this drug?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with moderate vascular dementia (MMSE 18) presents after a fall. His daughter reports more confusion and frequent falls. He takes donepezil 10 mg daily, amlodipine 10 mg daily, and trazodone 100 mg nightly, started two weeks ago for sleep. Blood pressure is 140/80 supine and 110/65 standing. Which medication change best addresses the timing of the sleepiness and postural symptoms?

Practice · An 84-year-old widower with vascular dementia (MoCA 19/30), hypertension, and stage 3a CKD (eGFR 52 mL/min) lives alone. His wife died six months ago and his daughter visits weekly. He has stopped bathing, wears the same clothes for days, has unpaid bills, and has only spoiled food in the refrigerator. Apart from poor hygiene, examination is unremarkable; BP is 142/88. He takes amlodipine 10 mg and donepezil 10 mg daily. Home-based primary care is being considered. Which description matches that model in Hazzard?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with Alzheimer dementia (MMSE 18/30), osteoporosis, and recurrent falls attends with her daughter. She has fallen three times in two months and takes donepezil 10 mg daily, alendronate 70 mg weekly, and vitamin D 2000 IU daily. Her daughter asks about memory drugs but appears exhausted and has had no break from caregiving for six months. Which intervention directly gives the caregiver time to maintain her own health and social connections?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman living independently has stopped hosting family meals and needs help with shopping, cooking, and medication management. Cognitive testing shows recall and clock-drawing difficulties. Examination and laboratory results are normal, and MRI shows mild atrophy. Donepezil has been started. Which additional approach directly evaluates her daily care needs and home safety?
Practice · When counseling a family about symptomatic medication for Alzheimer disease, which statement best reflects the evidence described in Hazzard?

Practice · An 82-year-old nursing-home resident with severe dementia, dysphagia, and pressure ulcers has lost 15% of her weight in six months despite speech therapy and nutritional supplements. Her family asks about tube feeding during a goals-of-care review. Her medications include donepezil, memantine, mirtazapine for appetite, and megestrol. Which prescribing approach best follows Hazzard's general principles?

Practice · A 75-year-old man with mild Alzheimer disease and stage 3b chronic kidney disease (eGFR 42) has increased evening confusion and two episodes of urinary incontinence. He takes donepezil 10 mg nightly, memantine 10 mg twice daily, and oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily, started one month ago for urgency. Examination is normal and urinalysis is negative. Which approach directly addresses a possible adverse effect of the newly added bladder medication?

Practice · A patient with Parkinson disease develops functionally important dementia after years of established motor disease. Which cholinesterase inhibitor has a US labeled indication for mild to moderate dementia associated with Parkinson disease?

Practice · An 82-year-old woman with moderate Alzheimer disease and osteoporosis becomes more agitated in the evenings, wanders, and tries to leave her assisted-living residence. She recently pushed another resident. She takes donepezil, memantine, vitamin D, and calcium. Vital signs and examination show no acute abnormality. Alongside assessment of triggers and immediate safety, which behavioral-care plan follows Hazzard?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with hypertension, BPH, and mild Alzheimer dementia collapses after rising to urinate at 3 am. He cannot recall the event and reports no chest pain or palpitations. He takes amlodipine 10 mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly, and donepezil 10 mg daily. Blood pressure falls from 142/78 supine to 108/68 after three minutes standing; heart rate remains 72. Which medication change best addresses the suspected cause of the postural drop?

Practice · A 79-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment on screening (MoCA 22/30) and hypertension attends follow-up. His daughter reports that he gets lost on familiar routes and missed two bill payments this month. Delayed recall is 4/5 and clock drawing is 0/3. Examination shows mild cogwheel rigidity. Blood pressure is 145/85 mm Hg, creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, and eGFR 52 mL/min/1.73 m². He takes amlodipine 5 mg daily and aspirin 81 mg. Which step directly assesses performance across cognitive domains to clarify the type and extent of impairment?

Practice · An 80-year-old man with moderate vascular dementia and atrial fibrillation is reviewed after a mechanical fall at home. His wife reports increasing confusion over the past two weeks and difficulty managing medications. He takes warfarin with a target INR of 2-3, metoprolol 25 mg twice daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. His INR today is 4.8, without active bleeding. After addressing the current INR abnormality, the clinician is considering a direct oral anticoagulant for longer-term stroke prevention. Which principle should guide this assessment?

Practice · A 77-year-old man with diabetes, heart failure (ejection fraction 40%), and mild dementia attends a geriatric clinic. His wife reports two falls in the past month, missed medication despite pill organizers, and inability to manage household finances. She works full time and feels overwhelmed. He takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, carvedilol 12.5 mg twice daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. HbA1c is 9.1%, creatinine 1.6, and eGFR 42. Which model explicitly uses protocols addressing medication management, falls, dementia, and caregiver burden?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman with diabetes, depression, and mild Alzheimer dementia attends a geriatric assessment. Her daughter reports missed medications and two hypoglycemic episodes requiring emergency visits. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glipizide 10 mg twice daily, sertraline 100 mg daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. HbA1c is 6.8%, and recorded glucose values range from 65 to 280. Which medication change most directly reduces the risk of another sulfonylurea-related hypoglycemic episode?

Practice · An 87-year-old man with mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 22/30) and hypertension is seen in the emergency department after a fall at his assisted-living facility. His daughter reports two other falls during the past month. He takes amlodipine 10 mg daily, donepezil 10 mg daily, and trazodone 50 mg at bedtime. Blood pressure is 138/82 sitting and 118/70 after three minutes standing. Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance is 42 mL/min. Which approach to his insomnia treatment is consistent with Hazzard?

Practice · An 86-year-old man with moderate dementia, heart failure (EF 40%), and stage 4 CKD (eGFR 24; Cockcroft-Gault CrCl 22 mL/min) physically resists care and has thrown a cup at another resident. He takes donepezil 10 mg, carvedilol 6.25 mg twice daily, and furosemide 20 mg daily. After assessing contributors and trying nonpharmacologic measures, dangerous aggression persists. If the risk-benefit assessment favors risperidone, which prescribing approach matches Hazzard?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with Alzheimer dementia (MMSE 14) and osteoarthritis has fallen twice in the past month without injury. She inconsistently uses a walker. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg four times daily; amitriptyline 25 mg nightly was added for sleep six weeks ago. Blood pressure is 128/78 sitting and 108/68 after three minutes standing; pulse rises from 72 to 78. Which medication change best addresses the timing of the falls and the postural pressure drop?

Practice · A 76-year-old man with moderate Alzheimer disease (MMSE 18), BPH, and insomnia has had worsening confusion and visual hallucinations of children in his room for two months. He takes donepezil 10 mg daily, terazosin 5 mg at bedtime, and diphenhydramine 50 mg at bedtime for sleep. Examination shows cogwheel rigidity and bradykinesia. Which change reduces the strong anticholinergic exposure identified by Beers 2023?

Practice · An 82-year-old woman hospitalized with pneumonia becomes irritable on the third hospital day, grimaces with movement, and resists care. She has moderate dementia, a positive delirium screen, and difficulty localizing her reported severe generalized pain. Temperature is 37.8°C, heart rate 102, and blood pressure 160/95. Her home medications include donepezil, amlodipine, and acetaminophen 500 mg twice daily for arthritis. While evaluating the new pain and delirium, the team considers acetaminophen as one component of treatment for her osteoarthritis pain. Which approach follows Hazzard’s discussion of this drug?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman with mild cognitive impairment is brought by her family for weight loss. She has lost 8 kg in six months and has a Mini Nutritional Assessment score of 19, indicating nutritional risk. She lives alone and says she forgets to eat. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily, omeprazole 40 mg daily, and zolpidem 10 mg at night. Laboratory results show albumin 3.4 g/dL and vitamin B12 280 pg/mL. Which approach follows Hazzard's principles for addressing contributors to poor nutritional intake?
Practice · A 79-year-old woman taking a stable dose of donepezil develops new delirium. Initial blood tests and urinalysis do not explain it. What is the appropriate next step in evaluation?

Practice · A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and moderate Alzheimer dementia lives with her daughter, who has discovered medication errors. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, donepezil 10 mg daily, and aspirin 81 mg daily. HbA1c is 7.2%, blood pressure is 145/85, and eGFR is 48. Which statement correctly identifies the source-described hypoglycemia concern in her oral diabetes regimen?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman is brought by her daughter for routine follow-up. She has fallen twice in the past month and seems more forgetful. She lives alone and manages her finances, but recently burned a pot while cooking. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily, amitriptyline 50 mg at night for neuropathic pain, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and atorvastatin 40 mg daily. Blood pressure is 128/78 sitting and 108/65 after three minutes standing. Her Mini-Cog score is 2/5. Which approach to amitriptyline addresses the medication concern identified in Beers 2023?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Alzheimer dementia has become more confused over three days. He lives in assisted living and has a baseline MMSE of 19/30. He accused staff of stealing a wallet later found in his drawer and now reports seeing children who are not present. He takes donepezil 10 mg daily, memantine 10 mg twice daily, and trazodone 50 mg at bedtime. Temperature is 36.8 degrees C, BP 140/85, and heart rate 78; urine shows 10-20 white cells and positive nitrites. Which feature most strongly supports delirium superimposed on his baseline dementia?

Practice · An 82-year-old man with mild dementia and treated depression has acquired a firearm for protection. His wife recently found him looking sad while holding the loaded gun. He denies suicidal thoughts and says he was checking the weapon. He takes sertraline and donepezil. Alongside immediate assessment of suicide risk, which action directly reduces access to lethal means?

Practice · An 82-year-old man with mild Alzheimer dementia takes donepezil 10 mg daily. He has increased confusion, two falls this week, and ten days of diarrhea and anorexia. Heart rate is 48 beats/min, blood pressure 138/72, and ECG shows sinus bradycardia; basic metabolic tests are normal. Which response to the cholinesterase inhibitor is supported by Hazzard's adverse-effect guidance?

Practice · An 82-year-old man with moderate Alzheimer disease and osteoarthritis has increased evening confusion and fell a week ago. He takes donepezil 10 mg nightly, memantine 10 mg twice daily, acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily, and amitriptyline 50 mg nightly for chronic pain. Which action directly addresses a strongly anticholinergic medication exposure?

Practice · An 89-year-old nursing-home resident with moderate dementia and osteoporosis develops agitation and pulls at his clothing. Temperature is 37.1 degrees C, blood pressure 156/92, and heart rate 88. He has not passed urine for 12 hours, and bladder scan shows 850 mL. He takes donepezil, calcium, vitamin D, and oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily, started three days ago for urinary frequency. Which plan addresses both retention and the suspected medication contribution?

Practice · An 84-year-old woman who lives alone and manages her medications was independent in basic ADLs until three days ago. Her daughter finds her acutely confused and inattentive. Temperature is 37.1°C, heart rate 88/min, blood pressure 108/62 mm Hg, and respiratory rate 20/min. She is oriented to person only and repeatedly asks when her husband, who died two years ago, will arrive. Medications include donepezil 10 mg, metoprolol 25 mg twice daily, and zolpidem 10 mg nightly, started one week ago. Which interpretation should guide the initial assessment?

Practice · An 86-year-old woman with heart failure, mild dementia, and osteoarthritis presents with weight loss and fatigue. After a fall, she moved in with her daughter. She takes furosemide, lisinopril, donepezil, and acetaminophen. She eats less and needs medication reminders. Her weight fell from 58 to 52 kg in six months; albumin is 3.0 and thyroid function is normal. Which approach reflects comprehensive geriatric assessment?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with mild Alzheimer dementia and osteoarthritis spends more time in bed, eats less, and has lost interest in weekly card games. She has near-falls when reaching, temporal wasting, loose clothing, and difficulty rising from the examination table. She takes donepezil 10 mg daily and acetaminophen 650 mg three times daily. She has lost 12 lb (8%) in six months; TSH is normal, B12 is 320 pg/mL, and albumin is 3.4 g/dL. Which exercise prescription best addresses her weakness?

Practice · An 85-year-old woman with hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and mild cognitive impairment has fallen twice in the past month and now needs help with finances and medications. She takes amlodipine 10 mg daily, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and donepezil 10 mg daily. Blood pressure falls from 150/85 supine to 125/75 standing; her get-up-and-go test is abnormal and MMSE is 22/30. Which approach addresses her multiple fall-risk domains?

Practice · An 88-year-old nursing-home resident with moderate Alzheimer disease has become withdrawn over two months, no longer joins enjoyable activities, needs prompting to eat and spends much of the day in bed. He has lost weight despite no identified acute illness. He takes donepezil, memantine and docusate. Assessment has not identified major depression, dangerous psychosis or aggression. Which initial approach fits management of neuropsychiatric symptoms?

Practice · An 81-year-old woman in assisted living is assessed because her care needs have increased. She has moderate Alzheimer disease, osteoporosis with a recent vertebral fracture, and urinary incontinence. Her caregiver reports new dependence in bathing and dressing, previously performed independently, and two falls this month. Her medicines are donepezil 10 mg daily, alendronate 70 mg weekly, oxybutynin 5 mg twice daily, and acetaminophen as needed. Which response to oxybutynin matches Beers 2023?

Practice · A 78-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension and mild cognitive impairment develops fatigue, difficulty shopping and a postural blood-pressure fall after starting amitriptyline for neuropathic pain. She also takes metformin, glyburide, lisinopril, amlodipine, atorvastatin and aspirin. Which change best addresses the new symptoms?

Practice · A 91-year-old man in supported housing with mild dementia (MMSE 22) has lost 3 kg over two months. Staff report that he refuses denture care and eats soft foods. His upper denture fits poorly, with marked ridge resorption and several denture-associated pressure ulcers. His daughter asks about implants. Creatinine clearance is 45 mL/min; medications include donepezil and metoprolol. Which principle should guide initial management of the suspected denture trauma?

Practice · An 84-year-old man with moderate dementia (MMSE 18), diabetes, and benign prostatic hyperplasia has daily urinary leakage for three weeks. He takes donepezil 10 mg, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, and tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily. His bladder is palpable to the umbilicus; anal tone is normal and stool is present in the rectal vault. Postvoid residual is 450 mL and creatinine is 1.8 mg/dL, up from 1.2. Which approach addresses urinary retention?

Practice · An 84-year-old woman with Alzheimer disease, osteoporosis and recurrent urinary infections develops agitation, visual hallucinations and insomnia after starting ciprofloxacin for dysuria. She also takes donepezil, calcium with vitamin D and regular alprazolam. Which medication-review principle should guide assessment of her acute confusion?

Practice · An 81-year-old man with Alzheimer disease (MMSE 18) is brought to the emergency department after two days of unusual behavior. His daughter recalls an unnamed constipation medicine. He is confused and has asterixis. Results are sodium 138, potassium 4.1, creatinine 1.4, and magnesium 4.8 mEq/L (laboratory reference range 1.5–2.5). His other medications are donepezil, memantine, and atorvastatin. Which statement about laxative safety supports investigating magnesium hydroxide exposure?

Practice · An 84-year-old woman with progressive Alzheimer dementia and an MMSE score of 18/30 takes donepezil. Which cardiovascular adverse-effect pattern is identified in Hazzard as potentially serious enough to trigger deprescribing a cholinesterase inhibitor?

Practice · An 82-year-old woman with mixed Alzheimer and vascular dementia, MMSE 16, and hypertension has been more confused for two weeks. She cannot clearly describe symptoms. She is afebrile, with blood pressure 156/84 mm Hg and pulse 78/min. She takes donepezil 10 mg, amlodipine 10 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, and diphenhydramine 50 mg nightly, started three weeks ago for sleep. Basic laboratory tests are normal except creatinine 1.4 mg/dL, previously 1.0. Which change directly reduces a first-generation antihistamine's anticholinergic burden?

Practice · An 86-year-old nursing-home resident with moderate Alzheimer dementia had three episodes of low measured body temperature (35.5-35.8°C) last winter despite adequate heating. Each episode improved with passive warming. His medications are donepezil 10 mg, risperidone 0.25 mg twice daily, gabapentin 300 mg three times daily, and docusate. Thyroid and metabolic testing is normal. While reviewing medications and other contributors, which principle should guide assessment for hypothermia?

Practice · A 79-year-old woman with hypertension and osteoarthritis has three years of worsening word finding and getting lost while driving. Her MMSE is 22/30, with losses in orientation, recall, and naming. She takes hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, and naproxen 500 mg twice daily; eGFR is 52 mL/min. While considering donepezil, the clinician reviews chronic naproxen use. Which statement supports reconsidering naproxen under Beers 2023?

Practice · An 84-year-old woman with colon cancer is three days after hemicolectomy. She pulls out her Foley catheter and becomes agitated when staff try to replace it. CAM findings include acute onset, inattention, and disorganized thinking. She takes donepezil 10 mg for mild dementia; electrolytes are normal and hemoglobin is 8.9 g/dL. Review confirms no ongoing indication for the catheter. Which step addresses this source of immobilization?
